sounds.intro: French spelling has many silent letters. Learn these sounds first, then the rest follows.
rows: say "ee" with rounded lips, like German ü
like "uh" with rounded lips, as in "fur" without the r
nasal "ahn": air through the nose, no n sound
gargled at the back of the throat

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: tu (informal): friends, family, children. vous (formal): strangers, older people, work, and always for "you all". Use vous when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Je becomes j' before a vowel: j'ai, j'habite. On is very common in speech and means "we".

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Most plurals add -s, but the s is silent. You hear the plural in the article: le → les, un → des. Words ending in -al change to -aux. Words in -eau add -x.

grammar.title: Avoir: to have
text: Avoir is also used for age (j'ai seize ans), hunger and thirst (j'ai faim, j'ai soif).

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: -er verbs, the biggest group. Drop -er, add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. The -e, -es, -ent endings are silent.

grammar.title: Aller: to go
text: Going to do something soon: aller + infinitive. Je vais manger = I am going to eat.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Order: subject, verb, rest. Adjectives usually come after the noun, but short common ones (grand, petit, bon, beau, nouveau, vieux) come before.
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Wrap the verb: ne ... pas. In speech, ne is often dropped: je sais pas. Before a vowel: n'.
Wrap the verb with ne ... pas: je ne parle pas. Also ne ... rien (nothing), ne ... personne (nobody), ne ... jamais (never). Before a vowel ne becomes n'. In speech ne is often dropped.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays
il ne travaille pas le dimanche
eel nuh trah-VY pah luh dee-MAHNSH

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Three ways: raise your voice (friendly), put est-ce que before the sentence (neutral), or swap verb and pronoun (formal).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: tu / ton / te for friends and family. vous / votre for strangers and work. With vous, the verb ends -ez.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: avoir (or être) + past participle: j'ai parlé, je suis allé. Future: aller + infinitive, or add -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont to the infinitive.
ex: je suis rentré à la maison
zhuh swee rahn-TRAY ah lah may-ZOHN

grammar.title: Commands
text: Use the tu or vous form without the pronoun: parle ! (tu), parlez ! (vous), parlons ! (let us). -er verbs lose the final -s in the tu form (tu parles → parle). Negative: ne ... pas around the verb.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: pouvoir (can), devoir (must), vouloir (want) + infinitive: je peux nager, nous devons partir, je veux manger. Il ne faut pas = you must not.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: à = at / to; dans = in; sur = on; sous = under; à côté de = next to; près de = near; à neuf heures = at nine.
ex: the book is on the table
le livre est sur la table
luh LEEVR ay sewr lah TABL
the cat is under the table
le chat est sous la table
luh shah ay soo lah TABL
the shop is next to the bank
le magasin est à côté de la banque
luh mah-gah-ZAN ay tah koh-TAY duh lah bahnk
the park is near the station
le parc est près de la gare
luh park ay pray duh lah gar
le cours est à neuf heures
the key is in the bag
la clé est dans le sac
lah klay ay dahn luh sahk

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: plus + adjective + que = more than (plus grand que). moins... que = less than. le plus... = the most. meilleur = better, pire = worse.
ex: grand, plus grand, le plus grand
grahn plew grahn luh plew grahn
petit, plus petit, le plus petit
puh-TEE plew puh-TEE luh plew puh-TEE
elle est plus grande que moi
el ay plew grahnd kuh mwah
Tachkent est plus grand que Samarcande
tahsh-KENT ay plew grahn kuh sah-mar-KAHND
